# edgecenter_websec_ssl_certificate (Resource)

WebSec SSL certificate: your own certificate that `edgecenter_websec_resource` uses through `ssl_certificate`. Certificates the server issues itself, such as Let's Encrypt, are managed by `edgecenter_websec_lecert`.

The API cannot change the certificate, the private key or the chain of an existing certificate, so changing any of them replaces the certificate. Only `name` is updated in place. The API does not return them either, and an imported certificate has none of them in state. The first apply after import only writes them from the configuration to state and sends nothing to the API, so make sure they are the ones the certificate was uploaded with: for example, compare `cert_subject_cn` and `validity_not_after` with the output of `openssl x509 -noout -subject -enddate`.

A certificate that resources still use is not deleted: the API would delete them together with the certificate, so the provider stops and lists them. To replace a certificate in use in one apply, keep `create_before_destroy` in its `lifecycle` from the start, so that the resources move to the new certificate before the old one is deleted, and derive its name from the certificate, because names are unique among the certificates of the client. The check does not see subdomains: a certificate moved from the old protection API can be attached to a subdomain, and deleting such a certificate deletes the subdomain.

Import with `<cert_id>` or `resource:<resource_id>`. `GET <edgecenter_websec_api>/ssl/certificates` lists the certificates with their ids, and `edgecenter_websec_api` defaults to `<api_endpoint>/v2/protection`. `resource:<resource_id>` imports the certificate that `edgecenter_websec_resource` uses. A resource moved from the old protection API keeps its id, and the id of `edgecenter_protection_resource_certificate` in the old state is that resource id, so the second form needs only the old state. A certificate the server issued is not imported here: import `edgecenter_websec_lecert` by the resource id instead.

## Example Usage

```terraform
provider "edgecenter" {
  permanent_api_token = "251$d3361.............1b35f26d8"
}

variable "certificate" {
  type = string
}

variable "private_key" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

variable "certificates_chain" {
  type    = string
  default = ""
}

resource "edgecenter_websec_ssl_certificate" "example_com" {
  name               = "example.com ${substr(sha256(var.certificate), 0, 8)}"
  certificate        = var.certificate
  private_key        = var.private_key
  certificates_chain = var.certificates_chain

  lifecycle {
    create_before_destroy = true
  }
}

resource "edgecenter_websec_source_group" "example_com" {
  name = "example.com origins"

  source {
    source = "203.0.113.10"
  }

  lifecycle {
    create_before_destroy = true
  }
}

resource "edgecenter_websec_resource" "example_com" {
  domain          = "example.com"
  source_group    = edgecenter_websec_source_group.example_com.id
  ssl_certificate = edgecenter_websec_ssl_certificate.example_com.id

  options {
    tls_versions {
      value = ["TLSv1.2", "TLSv1.3"]
    }
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `certificate` (String) The certificate in PEM format. When it holds several certificates, each starts on a new line. Changing it replaces the certificate.
- `name` (String) Name of the certificate, up to 255 characters, unique among the certificates of the client. Changing it renames the certificate in place.
- `private_key` (String, Sensitive) The private key in PEM format: `PRIVATE KEY`, `RSA PRIVATE KEY`, `EC PRIVATE KEY` or `DSA PRIVATE KEY`, not encrypted. It is stored in the state in plain text. Changing it replaces the certificate.

### Optional

- `certificates_chain` (String) Intermediate certificates in PEM format. Adding, changing or removing the chain replaces the certificate.

### Read-Only

- `automated` (Boolean) Whether the server issued the certificate itself. It is `false` for an uploaded certificate.
- `cert_issuer` (String) Common name of the certificate issuer.
- `cert_subject_alt` (String) Subject alternative names of the certificate.
- `cert_subject_cn` (String) Common name of the certificate subject.
- `has_related_resources` (Boolean) Whether a resource uses the certificate. Subdomains are not taken into account.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `validity_not_after` (String) End of the certificate validity period in RFC 3339 format.
- `validity_not_before` (String) Start of the certificate validity period in RFC 3339 format.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
terraform import edgecenter_websec_ssl_certificate.example_com 11
terraform import edgecenter_websec_ssl_certificate.example_com resource:12345
```
